answer: A stake-weighted reputation system makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a deposit that grows with the trust it claims, so spawning a canyon of sock puppets costs real capital. Earned reputation decays like an ember cooling unless the agent keeps doing verified work, and a shared lagoon of attestations from independent peers lets newcomers prove history without trusting any single witness. An attacker must therefore pay, wait, and behave - three costs a bot farm cannot fake cheaply.
